$comment: Mid-century Modernism art data. Lengths are in units of a 400 x 400 artboard (multiply by artboard short side / 400), or given as percentages. Colours are roles only; hex values always come from the product's Wada combination. Numbers are rules of thumb read from the period work in research.md unless a source is given.

line.$comment: The key line (black plate). Thin and even for contours, heavier for structural strokes such as branches, legs and ground lines. It is a printing plate, not a pen: it sits slightly off the colour plates (see shape.misregistration).
line.cap: round or butt; one choice per piece
line.join: round for contours, miter allowed on straight-edged figures

brush.$comment: Optional dry-brush line for one or two strokes per piece (Jim Flora, UPA backgrounds).
brush.taper: Starts at 100% width and ends at 30-60%.

use: Contour lines run around some shapes, not all: at most half of the colour shapes get a key-line contour.
Detail lines (legs, stems, whiskers, beaks) are straight segments, 1-4 per object.
A contour never traces its fill exactly: it is offset by the misregistration and may stop short of closing.
rules: Black or the combination's near-black only; never grey or coloured lines.
No calligraphic swelling except on the optional dry-brush stroke.
Line weight is fixed per artboard; do not scale strokes with objects.

shape.$comment: Flat cut shapes. Geometry is drawn with ruler, compass and French curve: most edges are straight lines or circular arcs; the rest are long, even curves. Sharp forms are always balanced by soft ones (MC6).

construction.note: Main edges snap to 15-degree steps; free curves have no more than one inflection each.

vocabulary.spec: Closed shape of 4-5 cubic segments with exactly one concave side; width:height 1.2-1.6; no sharp corners.
vocabulary.role: The big field shape behind the emblem (support colour).

vocabulary.spec: Two arms meeting at an elbow of 100-130 degrees; arm lengths 1:1.2-1.5; arm width 18-28% of arm length, tapering 20-40% to rounded tips (tip radius 2-4% of arm length).
12-20 points, inner radius 0.45-0.6 of outer, optional rotation offset; outer radius 6-12% of the short side.
vocabulary.role: Sun, sparkle of news or 'new', a seal.

vocabulary.spec: 4 points, inner radius 0.25-0.3 of outer; outer radius 1.5-3% of the short side.
2-3 ellipses (minor:major 0.3-0.4) rotated 60 degrees apart around a solid nucleus dot; line, not fill.
vocabulary.role: Science, energy, the modern. Once per campaign at most.

vocabulary.spec: Apex angle 20-45 degrees; base corners may be rounded 1-2 units.
vocabulary.role: Tails, crests, beaks, rays, hats, spires.

vocabulary.spec: Vesica (two arcs), width:length 0.3-0.4, on a straight stem.
vocabulary.role: Nature, growth; in pairs or threes.

vocabulary.spec: True circles are allowed (eyes, suns, dots, heads).

vocabulary.role: Bars for type panels and Bass-style wipes.

sharpness.rule: Points belong to small and medium forms (tails, crests, stars, boomerang elbows). Large field shapes are curved or round-cornered.

misregistration.$comment: Colour plates offset from the key line, as if the sheet moved between passes.
misregistration.direction: One direction for every colour shape in a piece (down-right is the default). The key line and type stay put.
misregistration.show: The offset reveals a sliver of ground between fill and key line on one side and lets the fill run past the line on the other.
rules: Never randomise the offset per shape.
Skip misregistration on UI and small icons (under 48 px): it reads as a rendering bug at small sizes.
Every sharp form in a piece has a curved counterpart of similar or larger size.
Shapes overlap in at most two layers (field shape, then emblem).

figures.$comment: Stylised animals and people: Harper's counted parts, UPA and Blair's flat caricature, Flora's angular figures kept friendly.

animals.recipe: Body as one arc-and-line shape, a tapered-triangle tail, one feature (crest, ear, fin) as a triangle, a circle eye with an offset dot, legs as straight lines.
animals.eye: White circle 3-4% of the animal's length with a black dot of 40-45% of its diameter, set off-centre towards the direction of travel.
animals.pose: Profile or three-quarter, never front-on; one clear direction.

people.limbs: Straight or single-curve limbs, tapering; hands as mittens or three-line forks; no bendy noodle limbs.
people.faces: Dot or almond eyes, a single nose shape, an optional line mouth. Expression from pose, not detail.
people.rule: People are caricatured by type of character (a busy cook, a sleepy cat owner), never by ethnicity, nationality or body.

rules: No more than three figures per piece.
Figures are cut from flat colour; the key line adds only details.

corners.$comment: Rounded corners for layout and UI around the art. Pixels at 1x for screens. Mid-century layout is squarer than Humanist Minimal: crisp panels, rounded buttons.

use.image: none, or a kidney or circle mask for one hero image
use.panel / type block: none; a slanted parallelogram is allowed for one label

corners.nested: An inner radius is the outer radius minus the padding between them.
corners.print: On posters, image boxes have square or 1-2% corners; let shapes, not boxes, carry the softness.

composition.grid: 6 columns on posters, 12 on screen; text takes 3-4 columns on one side, the emblem the rest.
composition.balance: Asymmetric: the emblem's visual weight is offset by the text block, not centred.
composition.diagonal: At most one dominant diagonal (a branch, a bar, a tilted shape) at 10-30 degrees.

placements.use: Emblem and field shape on the right two-thirds, often cropped by the edge; headline top-left. The default poster.
Bass style: one cut-paper emblem centred on a flat ground, title below or across it. Film, event and launch posters.
Girard or Blair style: a row of 3-7 small motifs across a band, repeated with variation. Packaging, banners, email headers.
Emblem enlarged so part runs off one or two edges. Social posts and thumbnails.

composition.pairing: Image and headline are a pair: the headline must not describe what the image shows; together they make one idea.
rules: Text never sits on top of a shape edge; give it clear ground.
Keep at least one margin between text and the emblem.

palette.$comment: Share of the visible area for each colour role, treated as a 2-4 ink print job. Colours come from the product's Wada combination; white is unprinted paper.

shape.from: combination support colour (or ink colour in 2-3 colour combinations)

key.from: Wada Black, or the combination's near-black ink role when light-mode inkUse is body

method: Start from combinations with three or four colours: they map naturally to ground, shape and accent.
Prefer a warm ground (ochre, orange-yellow, cream, apricot) with a cool shape (teal, turquoise, peacock blue), or the reverse; this warm-cool pair is the period's signature.
Check light-mode roles: prefer inkUse 'body' so the key colour can carry text; for 'display' combinations, set text in Wada Black.
Avoid combinations whose ground would be a large field of olive, khaki or brown unless the product's world makes them positive (coffee, wood, bread).
The accent goes on the emblem only. If the accent is low-contrast on the ground (accentOnBg under 2), give the emblem a key-line contour.

recommendedCombinations.why: Cream ground, teal shape, red emblem: the classic mid-century trio. Display combination: set text in Wada Black.
Orange ground with black key, like Bass's Anatomy of a Murder and Vertigo posters; magenta accent kept small.
Ochre ground, orange emblem, deep green key: an autumnal Harper palette with body-text contrast (7.1).
Red-orange ground with teal and an indigo key: loud title-card energy, readable key (5.1).
Ivory paper ground, olive shape, sienna emblem, slate key: quiet Eames and Lustig book-cover feel.
Bright yellow ground with teal shape and a navy key: optimistic packaging and children's-book palette.
Aqua ground, mustard shape, sienna emblem, black key: the atomic-age kitchen palette; black text at 10:1.
Pale turquoise ground with cinnamon and burnt sienna: soft, Mary Blair-like warmth.
Orange-yellow ground, peacock teal shape, sienna emblem, violet-blue key: the most complete warm-cool set.
Cream ground, teal emblem, russet key: Girard-like folk-modern warmth.
Ivory ground with deep blue key and sienna accent: restrained, bookish, Lustig-adjacent.

rules: No gradients, overprint blends, transparency or shadows.
Text on the ground uses the combination's text role (AA contrast), or Wada Black.

texture.$comment: Texture comes from printing and painting, never from lighting. Use on at most two shapes per piece.

dryBrush.use: Gaps of ground colour where the brush ran dry, along one edge of a field shape.

speckle.use: Tiny solid paper (or ink) dots over the ground, like cheap stock or a worn plate.

halftone.use: One-ink photos and the occasional shadow or sky; in palette colours only.

texture.grain: No photographic grain, scratches or fake wear; texture is a printing trace, not ageing.

vocabulary.$comment: Symbols the period used and what they usually say. Combine one from the product's world with one from the benefit, then build it with the shape vocabulary.

avoid.why: The period's most worn-out space-age prop and a startup cliché.
Period stereotypes; caricature by ethnicity (see research.md 5).
Use the shape only as an abstract atomic-age form, never as cultural decoration.

method.$comment: How to find the one emblem: symbolise and summarise (Bass), count the wings (Harper), then print it in few inks.
recipe: Write the one message in a sentence (W1).
List five plain nouns from the product's world and five from the benefit.
Pick or join two into a single emblem that could be cut from paper in under ten pieces.
Build it from the shape vocabulary: one field shape (kidney or circle), the emblem in the accent, details in the key line.
Add one atomic-age punctuation (starburst, sparkle or boomerang) only if it supports the idea.
Test: redraw it from memory after 5 seconds. If you cannot, cut parts until you can.

examples.ref: Bass, The Man with the Golden Arm (1955)

examples.idea: a trial that takes a story apart
the coffee that gets you going

checklist: One emblem, redrawable from memory after 5 seconds.
2-4 inks counting black; white is paper; no blends or transparency.
Colour plates offset 0.75-1.5% from the key line, one direction.
Every sharp form balanced by a soft one; points on at most a third of the outlines.
Animals and figures in 5-9 (animals) or 6-12 (people) parts; no ethnic caricature.
Texture (dry brush, speckle, halftone) on at most two shapes.
At least 35% empty ground; one diagonal at most.
